A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAUP/SORT research. All 15 pages of v2 and 19 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack experiments on ImageNet and RIST across three MLLMs, geometric visualizations, ablations and supplementary sensitivity studies.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds semantic-similarity measurements, approximation-error analysis, cross-model geometric validation and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: SORT retains normalized-space optimization, the cross-entropy-plus-margin objective, and the same masked update and clipping procedure. Equations 9–12 and Algorithm 1 are substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet and the same RIST AutoDriving and RoboTasking trajectories. The added diagnostics examine retained data and models without introducing another application task, population or deployment environment.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the Image Hijacks baseline and the same w/o NSO and w/o SSO variants in corresponding comparisons. Bailey et al. changes from its 2023 preprint citation to its 2024 publication; the relocated taxonomy table adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New diagnostic protocols measure within/between-class CLIP similarities, sweep input magnitude to evaluate linearization error, and compare four PCA-feature similarity regimes across models and 2–9 classes. Existing attack splits, ASR definition, decoding and perturbation constraints remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 newly quantifies RIST semantic granularity; Appendix F tests the validity of the local linear approximation; Appendix G extends geometric validation beyond the original five-class Llava visualization. Appendix H adds examples across six model–constraint combinations. These substantially expand the questions investigated by supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Section 6.2.1 newly explains that Figure 6's existing error bars represent variation across RIST trajectories. This clarifies uncertainty reporting; no additional repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: The original attack figures and corresponding empirical table values are retained. Substantial new diagnostic results include inter-class CLIP means of 0.68 for AutoDriving and 0.73 for RoboTasking (Figure 12), Qwen approximation error of 0.85 at alpha=50 (Table 6), cross-model subcluster similarities of at least 0.95 (Figure 13), and additional qualitative outcomes.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds a scaled-input formulation and explicit definitions of relative first-order approximation error and feature agreement in Equations 13–14. This is a limited mathematical extension for diagnostics; the original assumptions, decomposition and Theorem 3.4 remain substantively unchanged, with no new proof or bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: semantic-aware hijacking through one universal perturbation, SORT, RIST and empirical feasibility across three MLLMs. The headline 66% five-target Qwen result is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 already specifies a digital white-box setting and acknowledges approximate Taylor reasoning. v3 expands these qualifications into explicit black-box and physical-deployment limitations and an error-supported account of the theory's qualitative role. It also attributes RIST trajectory variance to environmental diversity and uneven semantic granularity.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly identifies PCA as the projection used for the existing feature visualization, without establishing a changed procedure. The introduction replaces the anonymous code-access reference with a named GitHub repository. No new optimizer hyperparameter values or hardware specifications are supplied.

R1.justification: v3 adds Radford et al. (2021) for the CLIP analysis and replaces the general Gemini-family reference with Gemini 2.5 Pro documentation. Most other reference changes are publication updates for existing works. The many-to-many attack positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 polishes grammar and terminology, updates affiliations and publication information, and adds acknowledgments. The former Appendix F discussion becomes Section 7, supplemented by limitations, while new analytical appendices are introduced. The central exposition and section sequence are largely retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual evidence with a semantic-similarity chart, an approximation-error table, a cross-model geometry plot and a full-page model–constraint gallery (Figures 12–14 and Table 6). The former Table 5 becomes main-text Table 2 with revised column labels. Existing Figures 1–11 are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 supplements v2's single-model geometric visualization and brief approximation caveat with quantified errors, cross-model checks and RIST similarity measurements. These additions strengthen evidential support and clarify the theory's qualitative limits. The improvement is bounded: the main attack conclusions remain unchanged, and the new diagnostics do not resolve the acknowledged approximation and deployment limitations.
